newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK watchdog posts handover risk management rules.
newsitem.headline: HK watchdog posts handover risk management rules.

text.p: Players on Hong Kong's capital markets will face stricter risk management measures over the handover period as Hong Kong marks its return to Chinese rule.
The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), the territory's regulatory watchdog, announced a raft of measures on Monday covering the Stock Exchange and the Futures Exchange.
It said the Futures Exchange's clearing corporation would increase margin levels from June 26 until July 3.
For example, minimum client margins for Hang Seng Index futures contracts would rise to HK$60,000 from HK$50,000 a contract, the equivalent of 1,200 index points, it said.
The Futures Exchange's clearing house would also make an intra-day margin call at 2.30pm local time (0630 GMT), it said.
"This will mark positions to the market to ensure that they are approximately fully margined as of the close of trading on Friday," the SFC said.

For stock options, the Stock Exchange's clearing house would calculate margins based on three-day volatilities, and would issue an intra-day margin call on Friday afternoon, it said, without specifying a time.
It said the Hong Kong Securities Clearing Company Ltd would enforce normal procedures, marking open positions to market at 11.00 (0300 GMT) on June 27.
Brokers with unfavourable mark-to-market positions of more than HK$5 million would need to pay their marks to the Hong Kong Securities Clearing Company by 2pm (0600 GMT).
Margin and mark-to-market procedures would return to normal after the handover.

Hong Kong reverts to Chinese sovereignty on July 1 after more than 150 years of British rule, and the occasion will be marked by three days of holidays during which the territory's financial markets will be closed.
